paths.description: Homepage and primary search entry; represents global navigation, consent, promotions, footer, and search form.
John 3:16 NIV passage; represents the core reading result, tools, recommendations, and long content template.
NIV version information; represents a content/detail and Bible-book-list template.
Impossible keyword query; represents loading completion, empty state, and recovery guidance.
Global Log In/Sign Up destination; represents account and authentication entry.
News & Knowledge route returned the same Content Unavailable template and was excluded as duplicate error coverage.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The preference probe matched dark mode but reported body background rgb(250,248,247), black text, and colorScheme normal; the dark passage screenshot remains light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens for surfaces, text, controls, and browser chrome.

findings.summary: Page and state changes use abrupt swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection across home, passage, and version templates found no view-transition rules or API markers; navigation is traditional full-page replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively add same-origin cross-document View Transitions and reduced-motion-safe directional cues for primary navigation.

findings.summary: Long reading pages have no scroll-state-aware navigation or reading-position cue.
findings.evidence: The passage is a long 2,582px mobile document, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress-indicator technique.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading progress indicator or scroll-state-aware compact header without obscuring text.

findings.summary: The initial privacy wall and promotion displace the core Bible task.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show a consent surface for 545 partners consuming most of the viewport, followed by a persistent promotion; Scripture/search is not visible initially.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce consent scope and copy, keep Reject as easy as Accept, and present a compact, accessible consent layer that does not crowd out the primary task.

findings.summary: The consent experience is implemented as a large role=dialog subtree rather than a native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence found [role=dialog] spanning 780×321px and no native dialog, popover, or details elements across the inspected templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for truly modal consent and native popover/details for transient disclosures, preserving focus, Escape, and platform dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Application chrome dominates the first viewport.
findings.evidence: Screenshots show consent, masthead, a bright sales banner, and a large blank ad slot before the search or passage content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer low-value promotional chrome and reserve a content-first first viewport around search and Scripture.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-driven rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across reusable search, navigation, passage, and version surfaces found no @container or container-type rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reused search/navigation/sidebar components while retaining a viewport fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too small even though keyboard focus is visible.
findings.evidence: The home probe found 11 of 20 visible controls below 24px in one dimension; the passage found 43 of 334. Focus received a visible 1px auto outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase compact icon and link hit areas toward WCAG 2.2 target sizing, preserve visible :focus-visible, and avoid hover-only meaning.

findings.summary: The primary Scripture search is hidden below consent, sales, and ad chrome.
findings.evidence: The first-view screenshots contain no search field or page heading; the home DOM has no H1. Search becomes clear only after consent and scrolling.
findings.suggestedFix: Put a descriptive heading and the passage/keyword search in the first content viewport, ahead of promotions and ad inventory.

findings.summary: The passage template misses good lab Core Web Vitals.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.8s and CLS 0.699 on the passage (performance 49); the home also measured CLS 0.699.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dynamic regions, prioritize the actual LCP content, and retest LCP/CLS under mobile throttling until LCP ≤2.5s and CLS ≤0.1.

findings.summary: Large late shifts make the page visually unstable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported CLS 0.699; the mobile layout observer also recorded a 0.816 shift after late UI changes. All 25 passage images lack width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for ads, consent/promo regions, and images; stabilize font and dynamic-slot geometry before paint.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking and poorly cached resources delay content delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR identified synchronous head scripts init.min.js and otSDKStub.js; DOM confirmed neither async nor defer. Numerous cover images lacked cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, keep consent bootstrap minimal, avoid duplicate CSS delivery, and apply long-lived immutable caching to versioned images/assets.

findings.summary: The passage ships substantial unused consent and template code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified about 122KB of OneTrust JavaScript and 19.6KB of consent CSS as largely unused, plus additional unused passage CSS/JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Load consent capabilities on demand, tree-shake template bundles, and split sidebar/premium features from the core verse path.

findings.summary: The passage has unnamed controls and invalid accessibility semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 84 and failed button-name, aria-prohibited-attr, list semantics, and accessibility-tree checks; the image audit also found a missing alt attribute.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon button an accessible name, remove prohibited ARIA, repair list ownership, and provide appropriate alt text or empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: Some text and controls fail minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed color-contrast on both home and passage, with concrete failing nodes recorded in its audit tables.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust semantic color tokens to meet WCAG AA in normal, dark, and high-contrast conditions.

findings.summary: Heading and list structure does not consistently match reading order.
findings.evidence: The home has no H1 and starts at H3; passage Lighthouse failed heading-order and list structure while finding a visible keyboard outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive H1 per template, use sequential heading levels, and keep only li/script/template as direct ul/ol children.

findings.summary: Reflow works, but target sizing remains inadequate.
findings.evidence: At 360px both tested templates had zero horizontal overflow, yet probes counted 11 small controls on home and 43 on passage.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain the fluid layout and enlarge hit areas without reducing text zoom or introducing fixed widths.

findings.summary: Image markup is not dimensionally sound.
findings.evidence: All 25 passage images lacked width/height and Lighthouse found an incorrectly displayed image aspect ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width and height (or stable aspect-ratio) and preserve each source image’s native ratio.

findings.summary: The version-information template lacks a meta description.
findings.evidence: The version probe found a descriptive title but no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise, unique description from the version name and visible version information.

findings.summary: Some homepage links are not crawlable anchors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO scored 92 on home and failed crawlable-anchors, although viewport metadata and most real href links were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for all navigational links; reserve buttons for same-page actions.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are incomplete across a multilingual public site.
findings.evidence: Canonical URLs were present, but /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 403 to the browser probe and no hreflang links were found on English pages despite an explicit Spanish version.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a crawler-accessible sitemap and add reciprocal hreflang/default annotations for localized equivalents.

findings.summary: Rich public content lacks structured data.
findings.evidence: The passage has accurate Open Graph fields but no JSON-LD; the version template has only a generic sharing image.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org JSON-LD for WebSite/SearchAction and appropriate CreativeWork/Article entities, aligned with visible content.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS were present, but the header audit found no CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP (including frame-ancestors), nosniff, a privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The consent cookie is not marked Secure.
findings.evidence: Cookie evidence found OptanonConsent on .biblegateway.com with Secure=false, SameSite=Lax, and a 365-day expiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on all production cookies and review whether a full-year consent lifetime is necessary.

findings.summary: The consent and third-party footprint is disproportionate for a text-reading task.
findings.evidence: The consent UI describes 545 partners and device-characteristic scanning. The passage transferred 851,512 third-party bytes (78% of 1.09MB), including 413,746 bytes from OneTrust.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize partner purposes and vendors, load only strictly necessary consent code before choice, and defer optional third parties until explicit consent and user need.

findings.summary: The advertised sign-in surface is unavailable, preventing a modern-auth experience.
findings.evidence: The prominent Log In/Sign Up link resolves to a “Content Unavailable” page with no controls; no permission prompt fired on the inspected entry path.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore the account path and offer passkey/WebAuthn sign-in with password fallback and correct autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses beyond HSTS are absent.
findings.evidence: The response had HSTS but no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP, or nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Add defense-in-depth headers, test embedding requirements, and consider Trusted Types for script-heavy surfaces.

findings.summary: The consent layer is a fragile, oversized custom runtime surface.
findings.evidence: At 360×800 the consent UI consumes roughly 650px before site navigation; DOM inspection found custom role=dialog markup rather than native dialog behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a bounded native dialog with robust focus management, overflow scrolling, Escape policy, and content visible around or immediately after dismissal.

findings.summary: The account failure state offers no recovery action.
findings.evidence: The login URL displays only “Content Unavailable” and an apology, with no retry, home link, support link, status detail, or alternate sign-in path.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide actionable recovery: retry, return to reading, support/status link, and a stable error identifier while preserving context.

findings.summary: Consent asks users to authorize unusually broad sensitive profiling before content.
findings.evidence: The full-screen notice names 545 partners, personalized advertising, device-characteristic scanning, and inference of religious or philosophical beliefs on a Bible-reading site. Reject is present, but the breadth and interruption undermine a privacy-minimizing default.
findings.suggestedFix: Default optional purposes off, drastically reduce vendors, separate necessary from advertising purposes, and make privacy-preserving use the effortless path.

findings.summary: Email input explicitly disables autofill.
findings.evidence: Home and passage probes show the newsletter Email field with autocomplete="off" and no visible label in the captured form metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email, a persistent label, and autocomplete=email; keep autocomplete off only where the task genuinely requires it.

findings.summary: Account entry is a dead end.
findings.evidence: Log In/Sign Up links users to a noindex “Content Unavailable” page with no sign-in, cancellation, recovery, or support controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a clear, secure sign-in/account flow with recovery and passkey support, then test end-to-end from the global header.

findings.summary: Below-fold imagery is delivered in legacy, unstable markup.
findings.evidence: The passage image audit found 24 legacy JPG/PNG images, 24 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 25 without dimensions, and nearly all without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Use AVIF/WebP where beneficial, lazy-load below-fold covers, provide srcset/sizes, and emit intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: The initial request graph fetches work unrelated to reading one verse.
findings.evidence: The passage made 76 requests, including 24 eager below-fold images and 26 fetch/XHR requests; 413KB of OneTrust resources dominated optional setup.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer recommendations, cover art, and nonessential consent/vendor datasets until interaction or idle after core content.

findings.summary: Third parties consume most transferred bytes.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 35 third-party requests and 851,512 third-party bytes out of 1,090,146 total; OneTrust alone used about 414KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, self-host or eliminate low-value dependencies, and gate optional media and vendor code behind intent.

taskList.title: Replace the broad consent wall with a privacy-minimizing, content-first consent experience
Stabilize dynamic slots and optimize passage LCP
Restore and secure the account/sign-in journey
Deploy CSP and the missing defense-in-depth headers
Repair accessible names, ARIA/list/heading semantics, contrast, and target sizes
Defer parser-blocking, unused, and below-fold resources
Put search and Scripture ahead of promotional chrome
Complete crawlability, sitemap, hreflang, and structured metadata
Add preference-aware theming and progressive navigation transitions
Modernize responsive component and autofill behavior
